title: Annotatio IV §.II (2): Lust of the eyes — excessive sacred curiosity; multiplies dogmas and unhealthy novelties
pass_a_gloss: (2.) By lust of the eyes — understand spiritual lusts, or of the soul; in one word, excessive Curiosity in Sacred things, sprung from ambition, against that word of the Apostle in Rom. 12:3, not to think beyond what one ought to think, but to think unto sobriety (for the inflated man languishes about questions — 1 Tim. 6:3–5 — which a Bishop must flee, 2 Tim. 2:23–24; Titus 3:9), about to breed two evils most hostile to Ecclesiastical Peace: namely an extraordinary multiplication of Theological dogmas; and an unhealthy doting on things newly invented.
pass_b_english: (2.) Lust of the eyes — meaning spiritual lusts of the soul; in a word, excessive curiosity in sacred things, born of ambition — against Romans 12:3: do not think beyond what you ought, but think unto sobriety.
For the puffed-up man languishes among questions (1 Tim. 6:3–5) that a bishop must flee (2 Tim. 2:23–24; Titus 3:9).
This breeds two evils most hostile to church peace: an extraordinary multiplication of theological dogmas, and an unhealthy doting on novelties.
source_text: (2.) Cupiditate oculorum, intellige Spiritualium, seu animae, verbô unô, Curiositate in Sacris nimiâ, ex ambitione ortâ, contra istud Apostoli ad Rom. 12, 3. μὴ ὑπερφρονεῖν παρ’ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν ἀλλὰ φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν (nam inflatus languet circa quaestiones. 1. Tim. 6, 3. 4. 5. Episcopo fugiendas, 2. Tim. 2, 23. 24. Tit. III. 9.), duo admodum mala, Paci Ecclesiasticae quam maximè infensa, progeneratura, dogmatum scil. Theologicorum multiplicationem eximiam; & noviter inventorum malesanam deperitionem.
notes: Curiosity in sacris; Rom 12:3; dogma-multiplication / novelties.
